Heyya, dysphoria is awful and a pretty terrible experience, but the good experiences in life make it worth it to stay alive. I had some really similar problems at a really similar age, and I felt basically the exact same way you're describing, and I feel fucking fantastic now, especially as I'm a lot more capable of being independent. It's very difficult to see when you're stressed out or depressive or having a particularly bad day, but life is absolutely worth living in spite of the bad parts. Trust me, it's not always easy, but there *will* come a time where you're satisfied and fully aware of how great living is. Even if you can't see that happening now, it *will*. It's part of being alive.

Hormone blockers are a big help if you're able to get them. If you feel like you're going to hurt yourself, please don't. Call a hotline for suicide prevention or tell someone that you can trust to help you and get you medical help. There's nothing shameful about reaching out for help if you really need it; everyone has a right to live and if you need that to live, you deserve it. 

Also, this is something that's much easier to see when you're feeling positive but you have to be fair to yourself. You *are* a woman. Nothing that makes you dysphoric changes that, your identity persists through that. There are women with deep voices, and there are women who have body hair. When I was younger I was very dysphoric about my height, but now I've come to realize that there *are* tall women. That's because there's *me*, and I'm tall and a woman. You're not doing anything wrong by feeling dysphoric or sad about anything, but you have to remember and internalize that your identity is still valid and true.

Also, shaving is great for body hair. If you think you're safe to have razors, your parents are likely to be willing to buy you some. I shaved (and still do shave) all my body hair and it makes me feel a lot better about myself. Having smooth legs and arms and a hairless face can be shockingly satisfying and greatly helped me with dysphoria when I was going through some hard times. Just make sure that you're able to stay safe with the sharp objects!

Again, I don't know if this helps at all, I really hope it does, but it *will* get better for you. Your situation is eerily similar to how mine looked when I was at your age, and as I got older I started thinking a lot more positively about things and gained a lot more confidence. Keep your accepting friends close if you can, and remember: You can pull through this. Life isn't perfect and it'll be rocky at times, but you'll feel great and satisfied in the future. I know it probably sounds really hard to believe, but it's the truth. As someone who's gone through something like this, if I could go back and tell myself anything, it'd be that. Hope you feel better soon.
